problem.name: Quadratically signed weight enumerators
problem.statement_latex: Given binary matrices $A,B$ and rational parameters $x,y$, evaluate or decide the promised sign of $S(A,B,x,y)=\sum_{b:Ab=0}(-1)^{b^TBb}x^{|b|}y^{n-|b|}$. The quantum result uses the matrix structure, parameters and sign-gap promise of Knill--Laflamme.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ quantum time for the complete promised sign problem, by encoding a real quantum circuit into the enumerator.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ quantum time for the complete promised sign problem, by encoding a real quantum circuit into the enumerator.

classical.headline_latex: $O(2^n\operatorname{poly}(n))$ direct summation, improved to $O(2^{\dim\ker A}\operatorname{poly}(n))$ by enumerating the kernel. The promised complete regime is $\mathsf{BQP}$-complete. For an implemented $q$-qubit, $g$-gate circuit over a fixed finite algebraic gate set, classical simulation also gives $\min\{O(g2^q),\operatorname{poly}(g)2^{O(w)},\operatorname{poly}(s)2^{O(s/\sqrt{\log s})}\}$. Here $w$ is a contraction width and $s$ is the size of the sparse bounded-fan-in Boolean encoding of scalar path counts at the required precision; gate synthesis and precision contribute to $g,s$.
